messages.subject: Using Pygments for Rcpp in Rnw
messages.subject_clean: Using Pygments for Rcpp in Rnw
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I see that render_jekyll() has support for pygments, but I'm struggling to find examples of using pygments when targeting LaTeX.

Is it possible to use pygments instead of highlight for LaTeX documents? I've looked for a hook to replace hi_andre() in knitr:::hilight_source() but my attempts feel rather hackish at this point.

If it matters, my primary use case is Rcpp chunks.

Thanks,
Michael

messages.subject: Re: Using Pygments for Rcpp in Rnw
messages.subject_clean: Using Pygments for Rcpp in Rnw
messages.body_plain:
You can use pygments using the minted package for LaTeX

https://code.google.com/p/minted/

You will have to tweak how your run LaTeX since minted requires you to enable some command line parameters.

Hope this helps.

Best,
Ramnath

messages.subject_clean: [knitr] How do i make my function accessible to all chunks
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

Please see FAQ 1: http://bit.ly/knitr-faq If everything is up-to-date,
please see if the minimal example below works:

%------------------------------
\documentclass{article}
\begin{document}

<<test-a, cache=TRUE>>=
f = function(x) x
f(10)
@

<<test-b, cache=TRUE>>=
f(5)
@

\end{document}
%------------------------------

You do not need to redefine a function in every chunk. Objects created
in previous chunks should be available to later chunks.

Regards,
Yihui
--

messages.subject: knitr output within prezi?
messages.subject_clean: knitr output within prezi?
messages.body_plain:
Hi!

I'd like to create an interactive poster (sometimes called eposter)
(i.e. http://www.ascb.org/ascbpost/index.php/compass-points/item/150-how-to-use-prezi-to-make-a-dynamic-eposter-talk)

in which some sections consisted of knitr output
Would it be possible to include output  from knitr
i.e. such as
http://rpubs.com/gallery/googleVis
or at least just including animated graphics
within prezi?
If not, any suggestion for an alternative to prezi that would let us do that?

The goal is that the user moves around the poster, zooms in wherever considered interesting and take detailed look
at the graphics, best interacting with them.

Thanks

Agus

messages.body_plain:
My guess is, no, that is not possible. From my quick understanding of
Prezi, it does not allow interactive content like googleVis (which is
based on JavaScript and Flash). The only "interactive" content that it
supports seems to be videos. Therefore it seems you need to make a
video of your interactive content.

Regards,
Yihui

and the general ones from yours in
https://github.com/yihui/knitr/blob/master/inst/misc/vignette.css

require(knitr)
require(markdown)
spin("myscript.R")
markdowToHTML("myscript.md", "myscript.html", stylesheet='custom.css')

Just 2 minor problems

spin("myscript.R", stylesheet='custom.css')

but I get all the page (not only the 800px) with color #EDEDED

Thanks a lot for this impressive tool. You get so much out of spin() with so few added codes.

Agus

# Section 1

messages.subject: Re: Output directory for knitr'd files in RStudio
messages.subject_clean: Output directory for knitr'd files in RStudio
messages.body_plain:
You can set the path to the figures directory globally by including the following chunk in your Rmd file.

```{r setup, echo = F}
opts_chunk$set(fig.path = "images/")
```
